pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Severe Drug-Induced Ergotism (St. Anthony's Fire) THE SMOKING GUN: The co-administration of Ergotamine tartrate with Clarithromycin, a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, leading to massive toxic accumulation of ergot alkaloids. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ergotamine is primarily cleared by the hepatic cytochrome P450 enzyme CYP3A4. When combined with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like macrolide antibiotics (clarithromycin or erythromycin) or protease inhibitors, ergotamine metabolism is drastically blocked, resulting in dangerously high serum levels. Ergot alkaloids act as potent agonists at serotonin (5-HT2A) and alpha-adrenergic receptors, causing severe, prolonged peripheral arterial vasospasm, tissue ischemia, limb necrosis, and central nervous system disturbances (psychosis and hallucinations). Treatment requires immediate cessation of the offending drugs, vasodilation (e.g., IV sodium nitroprusside or prostacyclin analogs), and full anticoagulation.
